why: A (universe 0) is theorem_15_2_2_hyp with the one-branch lemma exists_branch_interior, two continuity facts and the witness theorem_15_2_2_hyp_witness. The two statements differ in one hypothesis: theorem_15_2_2_hyp assumes in addition A.B.IsScFredholmSectionTame f (germ data in tame charts at every smooth point of X, a global condition, satisfiable by the witness), which B's hypotheses (f sc-Fredholm functor, Λ sc⁺-multisection, x interior and transversal) do not give, e.g. when X has boundary points without tame charts. With that hypothesis added to B, A ⇒ B is proved (A_to_Btame; the tame hypothesis is also what makes the sheet points smooth, via mem_smoothSet_of_eq). B ⇒ A is proved: B's U(x) is shrunk into a chart domain and away from the branches with sᵢ(x) ≠ f(x), and (1), (2), (a)–(e) restrict; the one-branch lemma, the continuity facts and the witness are not consequences of B and are re-proved outright from non-item lemmas. B is believed to hold as stated (the interior implicit function theorem does not need tameness), but deriving it from A would require that theorem without the tame germ hypothesis.
